decisions.reason: The reverse implication from graph-norm completeness to graph closedness selects one graph point in each shrinking ball, which requires Countable Choice in this library. The repair states that axiom and its exact use; the core equivalence is now proved topologically through the graph isometry, without an unlicensed sequence selection.

The rejected direct argument confuses density of the domain with density of the range: the zero operator makes x↦⟨Tx,y-y'⟩ vanish for arbitrary y-y'. Riesz uniqueness remains valid, and the repair instead uses ⟨x,w-w'⟩=0 on the dense domain, continuity, and x=w-w'.

Surjectivity and the lower bound for T+i make -i-T=-(T+i) boundedly invertible, so they establish -i∈ρ(T), not i∈ρ(T). The sign error did not damage the equivalence because either nonempty resolvent point suffices to prove closedness, but the displayed inference was false and is now corrected.

The formula (T-i)(T+i)^{-1} is not licensed until -i lies in the resolvent set, and the cited self-adjoint resolvent theorem assumes Countable Choice. The carrier omitted that hypothesis, so its defining operator was not well posed under the stated interface. The repair propagates the axiom explicitly.

The original step equated the vector Cx with a scalar integral against F_x, so it did not prove the load-bearing fact F({1})=0 needed for Cayley transport. The repair proves ran F({λ})=ker(C-λ) using the bounded-calculus quadratic identity in both directions, then applies ker(I-C)={0}.

The cited unbounded spectral theorem assumes H is nonzero, while this definition quantified over every self-adjoint operator and supplied no zero-space construction. The spectral-type formulas are nevertheless canonical on H={0}: E(B)=0 is the unique PVM. The repair states that case directly and declares the finite-measure decomposition dependency.

A1 restated the multiplication-operator theorem for arbitrary measure spaces, although that supplier assumes sigma-finiteness and an almost-everywhere finite real multiplier. The actual application to Lebesgue measure on R satisfies those hypotheses, so the example's conclusion remains sound after narrowing A1.

The definition asserts that every nonreal reference point supplies bounded resolvents by invoking the self-adjoint resolvent estimate, whose stated interface assumes Countable Choice. Without that hypothesis the displayed convergence notions were not licensed as well posed. The repair adds the exact inherited assumption.

Because this library has 0 in N, the original interval J_0=[0,c-1/0] was undefined, so the stated exhaustion could not literally be formed. Replacing n by n+1 produces defined increasing bounded intervals exhausting (-infinity,c), preserving the spectral-projection contradiction and all later uses.

The cited metric-convergence item only defines limits of N-indexed sequences and therefore did not define continuity of the real-parameter orbit maps. Since that continuity is the defining property of the carrier, the interface failure is fatal. The repair uses epsilon-delta metric continuity on R and H and supplies both weak/strong directions.

The sole cited convergence interface defined only N-indexed sequences, while the generator is a two-sided limit over nonzero real parameters approaching zero. That left D(G) and G without a licensed meaning. The repair gives the exact punctured epsilon-delta norm condition and its equivalent metric-continuity formulation.

The library indexes sequences by N with 0 included, so the original zeroth difference quotient n(f(x+1/n)-f(x)) was undefined and could not define a Borel representative. Reindexing by n+1 yields continuous, everywhere-defined quotients with the same almost-everywhere derivative limit and restores the Tonelli measurability justification.

reviews.reason: The repaired graph-norm dictionary proves both directions with the declared choice cost, preserves the closed-graph and Hilbert-space conclusions, and derives the core criterion by a genuine homeomorphism-of-closures argument.

The definition now derives uniqueness from equality of the two representing vectors' inner products on the dense domain. Continuity extends the equality to all of H, so positive definiteness forces the vectors to agree.

Step 2.2 now uses the library resolvent convention z-T consistently and obtains -i in the resolvent set from T+i. The closedness and kernel conclusions then follow exactly from A5, A2, and condition (5).

The repaired definition assumes and declares Countable Choice before invoking the nonreal-resolvent theorem. With both shifts bijective, every displayed Cayley identity, unitarity argument, kernel computation, and domain-recovery formula is well typed.

The point spectral projection is now identified with the eigenspace projection by scalar-measure norm identities, making F({1})=0 rigorous. The subsequent transport, domain recovery, operator equality, uniqueness, and converse were rechecked, and the stale recovery-step reference was corrected.

For nonzero H the repaired setup uses the spectral theorem; for H={0} it constructs the unique zero PVM and obtains three zero subspaces directly. The measure-class definitions and spectrum conventions are then meaningful in every stated case.

A1 now reproduces the supplier's sigma-finiteness and almost-everywhere finiteness hypotheses. Step 1.1 specializes them to Lebesgue measure on R and m(x)=x, so the domain, PVM, calculus, spectrum, and generator arguments are licensed.

The carrier and its manifest now assume Countable Choice before using the self-adjoint resolvent estimate. Thus every fixed nonreal resolvent in both convergence formulas exists and is bounded, while parameter independence remains correctly deferred to the later theorem.

Step 1.2 now uses J_n=[-(n+1),c-1/(n+1)]. Every interval is bounded and defined for n in N, the family increases to (-infinity,c), and a vector in a nonzero projected range yields the required strict contradiction to T being bounded below by c.

The orbit maps are now explicitly continuous from the usual metric on R to the Hilbert norm metric via the metric-continuity interface. Translation by the group law proves continuity everywhere from zero, the norm identity proves weak-to-strong, and Cauchy--Schwarz proves strong-to-weak.

The generator domain now has a complete two-sided real epsilon-delta definition, excluding t=0 from the quotient and identifying the value by continuity after extension at zero. The triangle inequality gives uniqueness, and common-parameter estimates prove the domain and generator are linear.

Step 3.1 now constructs the periodic Borel representative from (n+1)(f(x+1/(n+1))-f(x)). Each term is continuous for every n in N, the Borel Cauchy-limit construction is valid, and differentiability identifies its limit with f' almost everywhere, completing the joint-measurability and Tonelli argument.
